Abstract.AbstractText: The analysis of oral fluid (OF) and urine samples to detect recent drug consumption has garnered considerable attention as alternative and less invasive biological matrices. Indeed, several groups have demonstrated that efficiently combining microex-traction and ambient ionization technologies can facilitate the rapid determination of target compounds in such biofluids at trace levels (low or sub ng mL-1). However, there is still a need for biocompatible devices that can both be implemented for in-vivo sampling and easily interfaced with mass-spectrometry (MS) analyzers. This study introduces a novel solid-phase microex-traction-transmission mode (SPME-TM) device made of polyetheretherketone (PEEK) mesh that can rapidly detect prohibited substances in biofluids via direct analysis in real-time tandem MS (DART-MS/MS). PEEK mesh was selected due to its bio-compatibility, excellent resistance to various organic solvents, and, when compared to other polymer mesh materials, its ability to withstand relatively high temperatures (≤ 350 ºC). The meshes were etched via ion-milling and subsequently coated with hydrophilic-lipophilic-balanced particle-polyacrylonitrile (HLB-PAN) slurry. The robustness of the coated meshes was tested using two methods: first, by performing rapid vortex agitation (≥ 3200 rpm) in LC/MS-grade solvents; and second, by exposing them to the DART source jet-stream at typical operational temperatures (~250-350 ºC). Single-use SPME-TM devices proved to be robust and were therefore used to analyze the presence of drugs of abuse (e.g. cocaine, MDMA, fentanyl, metha-done) spiked in urine and OF samples obtained from healthy volunteers. Excellent results were obtained for all analytes under study; furthermore, the tests also yielded satisfactory limits of quantitation (median ~ 0.5 ng mL-1), linearity (≥0.99), and reproducibility (80-120%) over the evaluated range (0.5-200 ng mL-1). This research highlights plastic SPME-TM's potential usefulness as a method for rapidly screening for prohibited substances in on-site/in vivo scenarios, such as roadside or work-place drug testing, anti-doping controls, and pain management programs.

Article.ArticleTitle: Single Use Polyetheretherketone (PEEK) Solid-Phase Microextraction-Transmission Mode (SPME-TM) devices for rapid screening and quantitation of drugs of abuse in oral fluid and urine via direct analysis in real time-tandem mass spectrometry (DART-MS/MS).
